projects.name: 1.2.1.52 Inclusive, competitive and sustainable value chain development in agriculture, fisheries and forestry
projects.description:
The project focuses on increasing the competitiveness of the agriculture sector of Ukraine, including Fisheries and Forestry.   
The project aims to support the design and implementation of the correct policies and tools to develop and implement sustainable forestry and fisheries policies. In close coordination with the European Union technical assistance, FAO focuses particularly on the review, adoption, and implementation of the legal framework on forestry; the development of a sustainable forest management model; the improvement of the professional level of forestry employees; and support for the functioning of a nationwide, unified system for the electronic accounting of wood.
Related to fisheries, the project assists in the effective implementation of the national strategic plan and will continue working afterward on the revision and possible adaptation of the fisheries legal frameworks, in line with the European Union Common Fisheries Policy, while taking into account international obligations within the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM). FAO also will work on the management of fishing capacity/effort; the development of fishing control and monitoring tools; support for the country in combating Illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing;
Also, the project aims at improving access for smallholder farmers to services, inputs, and finance through inclusive value chain development. The improved competitiveness of inclusive value chains will be achieved by addressing two key challenges of smallholders: lack of financial management skills and lack of investment.

projects.description:
The Project will focus on two principal areas. The first is strengthening personal and community security through greater engagement by citizens and institutions in conflict-affected areas. This will entail supporting local authorities and local citizen initiatives, such as Community Security Working Groups, in their efforts to define key security issues and tackle them jointly.

The second area the Project will focus on is to improve mechanisms for conflict transformation through the provision of effective and innovative services. The Project will support efforts to create effective early warning mechanisms, while also assisting resolving local conflicts. The Project will also look to support other innovative services, including legal and administrative support to persons seeking compensation or remedy for damaged property during the armed conflict, and monitoring of court proceedings resulting from the armed conflict.

projects.name: 2.1.2.5 - Development of services providers' capacities and integration of GBV response services at the regional/municipal levels
projects.description:
The project aims at supporting the Government of Ukraine, including regional and municipal authorities, and service providers to make available and accessible, adequate redress, assistance and protection to women who are victims of violence, including women and girls with disabilities and those residing in rural areas. It will do so by adopting a set of essential services as per guidelines outlined in the Essential Services Package for Women and Girls Subject to Violence, Istanbul Convention and will specifically address CEDAW Concluding Observations on the Eighth Periodic Report of Ukraine. Development of a model for comprehensive specialised services in target regions will be supported through capacity development, technical assistance and knowledge transfer to local service providers. The project will support the launching of crisis centres for GBV survivors and outreach mobile teams. 
As part of capacity development for service providers, the project will extend training to work with specific psychological issues of families of demobilised military personnel, which have been identified as a group of growing concern in terms of GBV risk. 
Technical assistance and further training will be provided to expand the police response to GBV /DV and strengthening cross-referrals between police and other service providers (psycho-social support, legal, health).
The project will provide support to centres on free legal aid to improve the capacity, knowledge and practical skills of their specialists in providing legal assistance to victims of gender-based violence, and representing the interests of victims in courts and with authorities. This component will also cover capacitation, sensitisation and training for lawyers (barristers, counsels for the defence) working with the Centres for Free Secondary Legal Aid.

projects.name: 1.2.1.51 Emergency assistance to enhance preparedness for Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) outbreak in Ukraine
projects.description:
Ukraine is located at the intersection of several bird migration routes, therefore, there is a constant risk of the introduction of HPAI with wild migratory birds from the territories outside of Ukraine. During the spring and autumn migration period, and in years of abnormally warm winters, this risk increases significantly. 
Since December 2020, Ukraine has reported 16 H5 HPAI outbreaks, 13 in domestic poultry affecting mostly small-scale farms, and three in wild birds including hawks and swans. Apart from migratory bird involvement, poultry trade within and between countries is another major driver for HPAI spread and five of the countries bordering Ukraine have already reported HPAI during the current wave (Hungary, Poland, Romania, Russian Federation and Slovakia). 
Outbreaks of avian influenza have a significant impact on the poultry industry and lead to significant economic losses, due to the slaughter of poultry, the imposition of quarantine and other restrictive measures, a ban on international trade and additional veterinary and sanitary measures that result in additional costs. Ukraine is an important producer and supplier of poultry for the European Union, Middle East, Central Asia, and North Africa. 
Given the vulnerability of Ukraine to H5 HPAI re-introductions and further spread, the financial loses it causes to the poultry industry, and the insufficient capacity of the government of Ukraine to prevent and manage the outbreaks, the aim of this project is to support the government of Ukraine with building its capacity in preventing further outbreaks of HPAI through the accurate early detection and surveillance, accurate diagnoses, and increased awareness on biosecurity among the stakeholders.

projects.name: 1.2.1.29 - Conservation and development of dual-purpose cattle breed in the West of Ukraine
projects.description:
Cattle-breeding in Ukraine is dominated by household producers who maintain native and locally-adapted dual-purpose breeds. These breeds have been created and selected for suitable adaptation to local conditions, particularly the mountainous regions of Ukraine, and are kept for both milk and meat production. The structural changes that followed the independence of Ukraine in the 1990s had strong negative effects on the support and development of these breeds leading to lower-grade animals and production. To strengthen the livelihood options of the household producers and holders of these dual-purpose cattle, a support programme is needed to maintain the breeds’ genetic diversity and sustainable use. The Ukrainian Carpathian Brown cattle breed has been identified as important in the country and its support and development has both national and regional significance.
The Activity aims to prepare the concept and details of development programmes for the selected breed based on a solid assessment of the existing situation of genetic resources and its production systems. State-of-the art approaches will be used for phenotypic and molecular genetic characterization of the cattle populations concerned and their production environments. This require the collection of relevant data from a selected group of locations, producers and animals. The information collected will be documented and published. It will form the basis for the formulation of breeding development plans, addressing both the conservation and genetic development of the three breed populations, as well as addressing the non-genetic aspects of breed development. The plans will be presented and discussed for consensus-building with relevant stakeholders during national consultations. 
The ultimate outcome of the activity will be a conservation and development programme developed for the selected breed, based on phenotypic and genotypic evaluation and molecular genetic analysis.

projects.name: 1.2.1.53 Enhancement of the national phytosanitary system
projects.description:
Ukraine is one of the largest producers and global exporters of grain. It is in the top-5 of global grain exporters, supplying more than 45 million tonnes of grain yearly to the global market. 
Plant protection is extremely relevant to facilitating plant exports, as all exported plants and plant products must meet the phytosanitary importing requirements established by importing countries, in order to make sure that pests are not moved in international trade. Unfortunately, the spread of plant pests and diseases enforced by the changing climatic conditions makes this task more and more challenging.
The presence of plant pests and diseases have had significant negative impact on the trade of Ukrainian grain. 
Insufficient phytosanitary verification systems can result in hurdles to export, while appropriate phytosanitary measures taken in relation to commodities relevant for export can facilitate access to export markets.
A number of countries (e.g. the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the EU, China, Indonesia or Turkey) require that some products can be imported only from areas that are free of certain pests .While the effectiveness of export inspections in detecting pests is limited, especially when the exported lots are large, or access to them is difficult, identification and establishment of pest free areas (PFAs) could provide additional guarantees of freedom from pests of the exported plants or plant products.
Based on the existing market challenges, there is a strong need to assess the spread of plant pests and diseases in Ukraine and to establish pest-free areas which could contribute to stabilised sale and support exports from Ukraine.

projects.name: 1.1.3.8 - Ukrainian Government supported in the development of a municipal food waste reduction strategy and action plan in the pilot cities of Lviv and Kiev that are aligned with national policies and context
projects.description:
The Ukrainian Government sees 'Food Loss and Waste' as a contribution to organic municipal waste and expressed the Government’s high priority attached to a FLW reduction programme. 

The aim of the project is to assist the Ukrainian Government to develop a municipal food waste reduction strategy and action plan in the pilot cities of Lviv and Kiev, aligned with national policies and context. The municipalities, with technical assistance from FAO, will develop comprehensive plans based on the ‘food loss and waste (FLW) management hierarchy’. According to the FLW hierarchy, the recovery and redistribution of safe and nutritious food for direct human consumption is, after prevention at the source, the preferred option to tackle the problem of FLW. Organic waste management - FLW diversion and recycling (e.g. composting, energy recovery) is another important pillar of the FLW hierarchy.

projects.description: UNODC developed a training module on Gender Mainstreaming in Monitoring & Evaluation of HIV Services for Women who use drugs that was implemented in the format of the regional workshop for Belarus, Ukraine and Moldova in September 2018 in Minsk. In total, 45 participants representing CBO service providers, country programme managers, relevant Government authorities and other implementing partners, attended the workshop. The training curriculum combined different learning techniques, thus creating a balance between the theoretical knowledge and practice. Content presentations were followed by group work and plenary discussions. The workshop increased both knowledge and skills to monitor HIV services for women who use drugs using gender responsive methods and tools, to collect and analyse gender-disaggregated data and develop evidence-based action plans streamlining gender issues in HIV programmes for women who use drugs.  UNODC supported the survey to review gender sensitive policies and practices in prisons (July-August). As a result, a 2-day workshop to address the health needs of women in prisons was held in August in Lviv. The workshop was attended by 55 partners of MoJ, MoH, prisons from 11 oblasts. Jointly with WHO, UNODC organised the 3rd regional meeting (Ukraine/Central Asia) and built capacity for the study on community management of opioid overdose (SOS study/October 2018, Kyiv) and reinforced advocacy for OST. UNODC organized the national conference on Drug policy in November 2018, that gathered more than 200 speaialists from MoI, MoH, social policy, education, informational policy, NGOs, etc. Overall, for the period of 2018, UNODC has reached around 1000 specialists by capacity building and advocacy activities.
